newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-India's Dalmiya to be next ICC chief.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India's Dalmiya to be next ICC chief.

text.p: India's Jagmohan Dalmiya will be next chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) for a three-year-term after the retirement of Sir Clyde Walcott in June, India's cricket board chief said on Tuesday.
"The working committee has already decided on Mr Jagmohan Dalmiya," Raj Singh Dungarpur, president of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), told Reuters by telephone from Bombay.

David Richards, chief executive of the ICC, said on Monday in Kuala Lumpur that India would take over at the head of the ICC in June and had until May 31 to name their choice for the new post of ICC president which will replace the chairman's job.

Dungarpur said the Indian board's committee had decided on Dalmiya as the country's chosen nominee last month, before the ICC decided in Kuala Lumpur that India would name the next ICC chief after the retirement of Barbadian Walcott.
Dalmiya, who is currently the secretary of the BCCI, played a key role in organising the World Cup cricket jointly hosted by India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka last year.
A construction magnate by profession, he has also been aggressively promoting the idea of commercial sponsorships for cricket and taking the game to more countries.
The game is now played mainly in a limited number of Commonwealth nations once ruled by Britain.
The president's post was part of a new governing structure aimed at improving the management and development of international cricket, Richards said.
India were unanimously elected to provide the president until June 2000 at a special general meeting of the ICC on Sunday.
Australia were elected as successors to India after 2000. The Australian candidate would serve as vice-president from June 1999, before taking over as president.
